title: Spear-phishing with macro-bearing document
hypothesis: An employee received a macro-enabled document that delivered an initial stager.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName in ('winword.exe','excel.exe') | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ('powershell.exe','cmd.exe','wscript.exe')
rationale: Office spawn of scripting host is the classic macro kill chain starting point.

title: Phishing link via mail with external sender spoof
hypothesis: A spoofed external sender convinced a user to open a link and sign in.
queries: EmailEvents | where EmailDirection == 'Inbound' | where SenderMailFromDomain != SenderFromDomain
rationale: From-domain mismatch is a cheap spoofing indicator pre-DMARC.

title: Internet-facing appliance compromise
hypothesis: A perimeter device (VPN, web app, mail) was exploited before internal movement.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ('w3wp.exe','httpd.exe','nginx.exe','sshd.exe') | where FileName has_any ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe','bash')
rationale: Web/service processes spawning shells = remote code execution on perimeter.

title: CVE exploitation in DMZ web app
hypothesis: An exploit payload was executed in the DMZ matching recent KEV CVEs.
queries: WafLogs | where UrlPath contains '=' and UrlPath contains '../../../../etc/passwd'
WafLogs | where UrlPath contains 'cmd' or UrlPath contains 'exec'
rationale: Path traversal + command execution strings indicate exploit attempts against known CVEs.

title: Valid creds from prior breach
hypothesis: Credentials from a leak/stealer log were used to log into internal systems.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4625 | where Account in (knownBreachAccounts)
rationale: Spraying leaked credentials produces 4625 bursts before success.

title: Drive-by download from common website
hypothesis: A user browsed a compromised site that redirected to a payload.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteUrl contains '.zip' and InitiatingProcessFileName == 'browser'
rationale: Browser downloads of executables/archives from non-enterprise domains = drive-by.

title: Voice phishing callback
hypothesis: A vishing callback led the user to install remote-control software.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('teamviewer.exe','anydesk.exe','quickassist.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'http'
rationale: Remote-control installs with network URIs match vishing workflow.

title: Removable media infection
hypothesis: Autorun-style malware from an external USB executed on an internal host.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName == 'explorer.exe' | where FileName has_any ('autorun.inf','solver.exe','copy.exe')
rationale: Explorer-spawned odd binaries can indicate removable-media auto-execution.

title: Obfuscated PowerShell onbox
hypothesis: PowerShell ran obfuscated code to bypass detection on an endpoint.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'powershell.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains '-enc' or ProcessCommandLine contains '-e '
rationale: Encoded command = deliberate evasion attempt.

title: Windows command shell batch execution
hypothesis: An attacker chained batch commands via cmd /c.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'cmd.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains '/c' | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @'.*(&|&&|;).*'
rationale: Chained commands in one /c invocation are unusual for admins.

title: VBScript host use
hypothesis: cscript/wscript ran a script from a writable location.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('cscript.exe','wscript.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'Users\\' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'Temp'
rationale: Launching scripts from user-writable dirs = LNK/HTA chain.

title: WMI remote execution
hypothesis: A remote host executed commands through WMI process creation.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessName contains 'wmiprvse.exe' | where InitiatingProcessAccountName != 'SYSTEM'
rationale: wmiprvse spawning subprocesses under a user account = remote exec.

title: Scheduled task execution in minutes
hypothesis: A task was created and fired in under 10 minutes as an exec channel.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID in (4698, 4699, 4702) | let t = TimeGenerated | join kind=inner (SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4698) on Computer | where t - TimeGenerated < 10m
rationale: Create-then-run immediacy = execution not persistence.

title: mshta as execution bridge
hypothesis: mshta fetched and ran remote script.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'mshta.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'http'
rationale: mshta with remote URI is weaponized by default.

title: Malicious LNK in attachments/desktop
hypothesis: A user double-clicked an LNK that spawned PowerShell/CMD.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName endswith '.lnk' and FileName == 'cmd.exe'
rationale: LNK-sourced cmd = shortcut weaponization.

title: JS execution via cscript
hypothesis: JavaScript payload (download cradle) executed through cscript.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'cscript.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains '.js' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'http'
rationale: JS with remote fetch from cscript = downloader.

title: Direct syscall execution
hypothesis: A process used direct syscalls to execute, bypassing EDR hooks.
queries: DeviceEvents | where ActionType == 'ProcessStart' | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains 'NtCreateFile'
rationale: Ndless-process direct-syscall patterns only identifiable via kernel/ETW telemetry.

title: Rundll32 shellcode loader
hypothesis: rundll32 executed shellcode from a data URI or DLL.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'rundll32.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'javascript:' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'data:'
rationale: Rundll32 js/data URIs = shellcode loaders.

title: Service binary execution via sc.exe
hypothesis: An attacker created and started a service to execute a binary.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'sc.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'create' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'start'
rationale: sc create + start rapid-fire = service exec channel.

title: Bash/awk on Windows (WSL)
hypothesis: An attacker used WSL to run Linux tooling on Windows.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('bash.exe','wsl.exe')
rationale: WSL spawn of Linux binaries is a lateral/execution oddity on Windows hosts.

title: Registry Run key addition
hypothesis: An attacker registered a binary in HKCU Run keys for autostart.
queries: DeviceRegistryEvents | where RegistryKey has 'CurrentVersion\\Run' | where RegistryValueData contains '.exe'
rationale: New Run entries outside vendor allowlist = persistence.

title: Startup folder placement
hypothesis: A binary/script was dropped in the StartUp folder.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FolderPath contains 'Startup' | where FileName endswith ('.exe','.bat','.vbs','.lnk')
rationale: Startup folder writes require user-level write access — attacker footprint.

title: RunAs service persistence
hypothesis: A service was created that runs as SYSTEM and executes an attacker binary.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 7045 | where ServiceStartType == 'auto' | where ServiceFileName contains 'Users\\' or ServiceFileName contains 'Temp'
rationale: Auto-start service from writable dir as SYSTEM = high confidence persistence.

title: WMI event subscription persistence
hypothesis: An attacker bound a WMI event filter to a consumer for silent startup.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 5861 | where ProviderName contains 'Binding'
rationale: New WMI bindings are rare and typically malicious.

title: Shortcut (.lnk) modification for autostart
hypothesis: An existing autostart shortcut was repointed to attacker code.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName endswith '.lnk' | where FolderPath contains 'Startup' or FolderPath contains 'Programs' | where ActionType == 'FileCreated'
rationale: Standard location shortcut rewrites match shortcut hijack.

title: Image File Execution Options debugger
hypothesis: An attacker registered a debugger for a system binary to hijack execution.
queries: DeviceRegistryEvents | where RegistryKey contains 'Image File Execution Options' | where RegistryValueName == 'Debugger'
rationale: IFEO Debugger for non-debug binaries = classic hijack.

title: AppInit_DLLs
hypothesis: AppInit_DLLs was set to load attacker DLL into processes.
queries: DeviceRegistryEvents | where RegistryKey contains 'Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Windows' | where RegistryValueName == 'AppInit_DLLs'
rationale: AppInit_DLLs registry load = legacy DLL persistence.

title: Kernel driver autostart
hypothesis: A kernel driver was installed with autostart service.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 7045 | where ServiceType contains 'kernel' | where ServiceFileName contains '\\Windows\\System32\\drivers' | where ServiceFileName !contains '\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\' and length(ServiceFileName) > 100
rationale: Signed-driver abuse (e.g. vulnerable cert) persists at kernel level.

title: Task with SYSTEM privileges
hypothesis: A scheduled task was registered to run with highest privileges.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4698 | where TaskContent contains '<RunLevel>HighestAvailable</RunLevel>' | where TaskContent contains 'Users\\' or TaskContent contains 'Temp'
rationale: HighestAvailable run level + writable path = privilege persistence.

title: authorized_keys write (Linux)
hypothesis: An attacker appended an SSH key to a user's authorized_keys.
queries: AuditdLogs | where type == 'PATH' | where name endswith 'authorized_keys' | where op != 'removed_attr'
rationale: authorized_keys modifications are high-signal persistence events.

title: winlogon shell key change
hypothesis: The winlogon shell was changed to include attacker binary.
queries: DeviceRegistryEvents | where RegistryKey contains 'Winlogon' | where RegistryValueName == 'Shell' | where RegistryValueData != 'explorer.exe'
rationale: winlogon Shell deviation = interactive-session persistence.

title: Undocumented local account
hypothesis: A local account was created outside identity management process.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4720 | where AccountName !endswith '$' | where AccountName !in (knownAccounts)
rationale: Local account creation without IT ticket = backdoor.

title: ScreenSaver binary hijack
hypothesis: ScreenSaver key points to an attacker binary.
queries: DeviceRegistryEvents | where RegistryKey contains 'Control Panel\\Desktop' | where RegistryValueName == 'SCRNSAVE.EXE' | where RegistryValueData !contains '\\Windows\\System32'
rationale: Non-system screensaver path = odd-but-cheap persistence.

title: DLL search order hijack
hypothesis: A writable dir was placed before system dirs in search order with attacker DLL.
queries: DeviceImageLoadEvents | where FileName endswith '.dll' | where FolderPath contains 'Users\\' | where InitiatingProcessFileName in (signedApps)
rationale: Authenticated app loading user-written DLL = sideloading.

title: COM object hijacking
hypothesis: A HKCU CLSID override redirects COM activation to attacker DLL.
queries: DeviceRegistryEvents | where RegistryKey contains 'CLSID\\{0002DF01-0000-0000-C000-000000000046}' or RegistryKey contains 'TreatAs'
rationale: CLSID overrides with InprocServer32 pointing to writable paths.

title: WinLogon notify/LogonScript
hypothesis: Logon scripts or notify packages execute attacker code at logon.
queries: DeviceRegistryEvents | where RegistryKey contains 'Winlogon\\Notify' | where RegistryValueName == 'DllName'
rationale: Notify package additions = early logon execution.

title: Exploitation of privilege-escalation CVE
hypothesis: A local privilege escalation CVE (from KEV list) was exploited on an endpoint.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'wevtutil.exe' or FileName == 'cmd.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains '/c' | where InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel == 'Medium' and FinalProcessIntegrityLevel == 'High'
rationale: Medium→High integrity jump via cmd = exploitation marker.

title: Token manipulation
hypothesis: A process duplicated a SYSTEM token to elevate privileges.
queries: DeviceEvents | where ActionType has 'Token' | where InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel != 'System'
rationale: Token duplication by low-integrity process = token theft.

title: UAC bypass via fodhelper
hypothesis: An attacker used fodhelper fringe-value bypass to elevate.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName == 'fodhelper.exe' | where FileName == 'cmd.exe'
rationale: fodhelper (auto-elevate) spawning shell = UAC bypass.

title: sudo misconfig (Linux)
hypothesis: An attacker abused a sudoers entry to run commands as root.
queries: SecurityEvent | where Channel contains 'auth' | where CommandLine contains 'sudo' | where User == 'root'
rationale: sudo escalation with unexpected command = misconfig abuse.

title: DLL injection into elevated process
hypothesis: A low-integrity process injected a thread into a System process.
queries: DeviceEvents | where ActionType == 'CreateRemoteThread' | where InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel == 'Low' and TargetProcessName in (systemProcessNames)
rationale: Cross-integrity CreateRemoteThread = injection into higher privilege.

title: Startup folder as admin
hypothesis: An attacker dropped a binary into the Startup folder to regain admin context.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FolderPath contains '\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\StartUp' | where FileName endswith ('.exe','.bat')
rationale: All-users startup writes mean admin had already been achieved.

title: Service binary replacement
hypothesis: An existing service binary was replaced with attacker executable.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FolderPath contains '\\Program Files' | where ActionType == 'FileModified' | where InitiatingProcessFileName == 'cmd.exe'
rationale: Repointing service binaries to temp files = privileged exec path.

title: CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP privilege use
hypothesis: A process was spawned with a privilege token it shouldn't have.
queries: DeviceEvents | where ActionType == 'ProcessStart' | where InitiatingProcessPrivileges contains 'SeDebugPrivilege' or 'SeImpersonatePrivilege'
rationale: SeDebug/SeImpersonate are the classic potato-chain enabling privileges.

title: File deletion of security artifacts
hypothesis: An attacker deleted evidence files (logs, tool records, cmd history).
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName has_any ('.log','.evtx','history','Recent') | where ActionType == 'FileDeleted' | where count() by InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(TimeGenerated,5m) >= 20
rationale: Bulk deletion of history/logs = anti-forensics.

title: Event log clearing
hypothesis: Security/System log was cleared to remove attack traces.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 1102
DeviceEvents | where ActionType has 'Delete' and FileName contains '.evtx'
rationale: Log clearing events are direct evidence of tampering.

title: EDR/AV service stop
hypothesis: An attacker stopped security agent services.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 7036 | where AccountName contains 'sensor' or AccountName contains 'defender' | where EventType == 'stopped'
rationale: Security agent stop = preventive evasion.

title: Firewall rule removal
hypothesis: An attacker disabled firewall rules to open egress/ingress.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'netsh.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'delete' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'set profile state off'
rationale: netsh firewall disable = C2 enabling step.

title: Sandbox detection (sleep/CPU checks)
hypothesis: Malware slept or performed CPU/RAM checks to evade sandboxing.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('powershell.exe','cmd.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'Start-Sleep' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'ping -n ' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'timeout'
rationale: Long sleeps before behavior = sandbox evasion.

title: Binary packing detection
hypothesis: A packed/obfuscated binary was dropped and executed.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName endswith '.exe' | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains 'Temp' | project SHA256 | join kind=inner (DeviceProcessEvents) on SHA256 | where ProcessIntegrityLevel == 'Medium'
rationale: Fresh-sha temp exe = packer/obfuscation candidate; verify with VT query.

title: Hidden file/system attribute set
hypothesis: An attacker marked files hidden with attrib +h to avoid casual discovery.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'attrib.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains '+h' or ProcessCommandLine contains '+s'
rationale: attrib hiding of fresh files = stealth.

title: Trusted publisher cert abuse
hypothesis: An attacker signed code with a stolen/abused trusted certificate.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where SigningStatus != 'Valid' and ProcessIntegrityLevel == 'System'
rationale: System-level unsigned/suspicious-signed binaries warrant review.

title: Clear PowerShell console history
hypothesis: An attacker cleared PowerShell history to hide commands.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'powershell.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'history' and ProcessCommandLine contains 'clear'
rationale: History clearing combos with early execution = cover-up.

title: Domain trust discovery
hypothesis: An attacker enumerated domain trusts for cross-domain jumps.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4688 | where ProcessName == 'cmd.exe' and CommandLine contains 'nltest /trusted_domains'
rationale: nltest trust enumeration = recon for cross-domain attack.

title: Registry modification for evasion
hypothesis: An attacker modified Defender/EDR registry settings.
queries: DeviceRegistryEvents | where RegistryKey contains 'Windows Defender\\Exclusions' or RegistryKey contains 'DisableAntiSpyware'
rationale: AV-disable registry writes are unambiguous evasion.

title: Indirect command via utilities
hypothesis: An attacker used odd utilities (forfiles, wmic word) to run commands indirectly.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('forfiles.exe','wmic.exe','bitsadmin.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains '/c ' and ProcessCommandLine contains 'cmd'
rationale: Indirect command execution via transfer utilities.

title: Masquerading as system binary name
hypothesis: An attacker copied a binary under a system name in a writable path.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('svchost.exe','rundll32.exe','lsass.exe','explorer.exe') | where FolderPath contains 'Users\\' or FolderPath contains 'Temp'
rationale: System-named binaries outside System32 = masquerading.

title: Deobfuscation step (certutil decode)
hypothesis: certutil decoded an encoded payload to disk.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'certutil.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains '-decode'
rationale: certutil decode of exe content = payload restore.

title: CLFS/event log tampering
hypothesis: System .evtx logs were edited/deleted by other than 'wevtutil' expected patterns.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName endswith '.evtx' | where ActionType in ('FileModified','FileDeleted') | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in ('wsmprovhost.exe','winlogon.exe')
rationale: Non-standard writers of .evtx = log tampering.

title: ADS (Alternate Data Stream) use
hypothesis: An attacker hid a payload in an NTFS ADS stream.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName contains ':' | where ActionType == 'FileCreated'
rationale: Colon streams = ADS storage of payload/scripts.

title: LSASS process memory read
hypothesis: A non-system process read LSASS memory to extract credentials.
queries: DeviceEvents | where ActionType == 'OpenProcessApiCall' | where TargetProcessName == 'lsass.exe' | where ProcessAccessRightFlags contains 'VM_READ'
rationale: ProcessAccess VM_READ on lsass = mimikatz/creddump.

title: SAM hive exfiltration
hypothesis: An attacker copied SAM/SYSTEM hives for offline password extraction.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName has_any ('sam','system','security') | where FolderPath contains '\\config\\' | where ActionType == 'FileCreated' or ActionType == 'FileCopied'
rationale: Registry hive copies to writable dirs = hash dump.

title: ntds.dit access
hypothesis: A DC's ntds.dit was accessed/copied (DCSync or offline).
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName == 'ntds.dit' | where ActionType in ('FileAccessed','FileCopied','FileCreated')
rationale: ntds.dit copies = full domain credential theft.

title: RC4 service tickets (Kerberoasting)
hypothesis: An account requested RC4 service tickets to crack SPN passwords.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4769 | where TicketEncryptionType == '0x17' | where ServiceName !endswith '$'
rationale: 0x17 encryption on service tickets = kerberoasting.

title: AS-REP roasting
hypothesis: An account with pre-auth disabled requested TGTs without pre-auth.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4768 | where PreAuthenticationType == 0
rationale: Pre-auth type 0 = roastable account probing.

title: Browser credential store access
hypothesis: An attacker read browser login data stores.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName has_any ('Login Data','logins.json','Cookies') | where ActionType == 'FileAccessed' | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'chrome.exe' and InitiatingProcessFileName != 'firefox.exe'
rationale: Non-browser processes reading browser vault = credential theft.

title: Credential files in user profiles
hypothesis: An attacker searched for passwords in user files (txt, ini, config).
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName in ('reg.exe','findstr.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'password' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'passwd'
rationale: findstr credential sweeps in profiles = classic password mining.

title: Unattended.xml/powershell profile with creds
hypothesis: Deployment scripts or shell profiles contain plaintext credentials read by attacker.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName has_any ('unattended.xml','sysprep.xml') | where ActionType == 'FileAccessed'
rationale: unattended.xml holds admin creds — access = theft.

title: Replication of directory changes (DCSync)
hypothesis: An account requested directory replication (DCSync) from the DC.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4662 | where OperationType == 'Control Access' | where ObjectName startswith 'Replicating Directory Changes'
rationale: DS-Replication-Get-Changes beyond legit sync tools = DCSync.

title: Credential stuffing on internal apps
hypothesis: Attackers used breached passwords against internal apps (VPN, webmail).
queries: SigninLogs | where ResultType == '50053' or ResultType == '50126' | summarize count() by UserPrincipalName | where count_ > 10
rationale: Repeated failed logins with common passwords = stuffing.

title: Keylogger module loaded
hypothesis: A module that hooks keyboard input was loaded into processes.
queries: DeviceImageLoadEvents | where FileName contains 'hook' or FileName contains 'keylog' | where FolderPath contains 'Users\\' or FolderPath contains 'Temp'
rationale: Custom hook/keylog DLL names in writable paths.

title: Kerberos ticket use from non-DC host
hypothesis: A host used a Kerberos ticket for admin services without requesting TGT.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4769 | where ServiceName startswith 'cifs/' or ServiceName startswith 'ldap/' | where AccountName !endswith '$' | where IpAddress !in (legitAdminIPs)
rationale: Passed golden/silver tickets hit cifs/ldap service tickets directly.

title: Vault/DPAPI access
hypothesis: An attacker accessed Windows DPAPI vault or secrets.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'cmd.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'dpapi' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'vaultcmd'
rationale: Manual DPAPI/vault commands = secret extraction attempt.

title: Web portal credential prompt (phishing page)
hypothesis: An attacker stood up a local prompt page to harvest credentials.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName in ('chrome.exe','msedge.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'file://' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'data:text/html'
rationale: Local html file open = credential-phishing page.

title: krbtgt hash request
hypothesis: krbtgt accounts were used for sign-on outside expected KDC flows.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID in (4768, 4769) | where AccountName == 'krbtgt'
rationale: krbtgt direct use = golden ticket attempt.

title: RDP brute force
hypothesis: An RDP endpoint was brute-forced with common passwords.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4625 | where LogonType == 10 | summarize count() by IpAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m) | where count_ >= 20
rationale: RDP login failure storms = brute force.

title: Account enumeration
hypothesis: An attacker enumerated users/groups to map the domain.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'net user /domain' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'net group /domain' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'Get-ADUser'
rationale: Bulk user/group enumeration = discovery phase.

title: Hostname enumeration
hypothesis: An attacker mapped internal hosts by name.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'net view /domain' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'Get-ADComputer'
rationale: Host inventory queries = lateral prep.

title: Group membership discovery
hypothesis: An attacker queried admin group memberships to find escalation targets.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'net localgroup administrators' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'Get-ADGroupMember'
rationale: Privileged-group enumeration is standard post-exploitation recon.

title: System information gathering
hypothesis: An attacker collected host info (OS, patches, AV) for exploit matching.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ('systeminfo','whoami /all','tasklist') | where count() by InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(TimeGenerated,1h) >= 5
rationale: Batch systeminfo/tasklist loops = fingerprinting.

title: Peripheral device discovery
hypothesis: An attacker queried attached devices (memory, disk) for later theft.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'wmic' and ProcessCommandLine contains 'logicaldisk'
rationale: wmic logicaldisk queries from non-admin = peripheral recon.

title: Network service scan
hypothesis: An attacker scanned internal subnets for listening services.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where ActionType == 'ConnectionAttempt' | where RemotePort in (445, 3389, 22, 8080) | where LocalPort != RemotePort | summarize count() by RemoteIP | where count_ > 100
rationale: High-volume connection attempts = port scanning.

title: Network configuration discovery
hypothesis: An attacker read network config to plan C2 routing.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ('ipconfig /all','route print','arp -a','netsh wlan show')
rationale: Network config queries from odd hosts.

title: File/directory discovery
hypothesis: An attacker enumerated interesting files (docs, configs, keys).
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ('dir /s','Get-ChildItem -Recurse') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'Users' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'AppData'
rationale: Deep recursive listing of user dirs = data discovery.

title: Time-based evasion (long baseline)
hypothesis: Malware waited days before acting (time-based evasion).
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where TimeGenerated between (now(-10d) .. now()) | where InitiatingProcessFileName == 'rundll32.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'svchost'
rationale: Long-delay first activity from dropper = time evasion.

title: Registry discovery
hypothesis: An attacker queried registry for config/secrets.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'reg.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'query' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'CurrentVersion\\Run' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'Winlogon'
rationale: Enumeration of autostart keys = persistence recon.

title: Security software discovery
hypothesis: An attacker mapped the security stack to choose evasion.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ('sc query','WMIC Product','Get-WmiObject') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'defender' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'sensor' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'edr'
rationale: Security-product queries = AV selection for blind spots.

title: Cloud account enumeration
hypothesis: An attacker enumerated cloud IAM users/roles.
queries: AWSCloudTrail | where EventName has_any ('ListUsers','GetRole','ListRoles','ListAttachedUserPolicies') | where UserIdentity.userName != 'admin'
rationale: IAM enumeration from non-admin identity.

title: SMB ADMIN$ access pattern
hypothesis: An attacker used SMB admin shares to move laterally.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 5140 | where ShareName == 'ADMIN$' | where AccountName !endswith '$'
rationale: ADMIN$ access with user account = PsExec/WMI-adjacent movement.

title: RDP session chaining
hypothesis: An attacker chained RDP sessions across hosts (pivot).
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4624 | where LogonType == 10 | let src = IpAddress | join kind=inner (SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4624 | where LogonType == 10) on Computer | where IpAddress == src
rationale: Host A→B→C RDP logons in sequence = pivot chain.

title: Admin share file staging
hypothesis: An attacker copied executables to admin shares.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 5145 | where RelativeTargetName matches regex @'ADMIN\$.*\.(exe|dll|ps1|bat)$'
rationale: Share writes of binaries = movement staging.

title: Software deployment tool abuse
hypothesis: An attacker used the software deployment platform for executable push.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'psexec.exe' or FileName == 'paexec.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains '\\' and ProcessCommandLine contains ' -s'
rationale: psexec -s remote push = movement/exec channel.

title: Session hijack (RDP tsclient)
hypothesis: An attacker hijacked an RDP session via tsclient share.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'tsclient'
rationale: tsclient access = clipboard/drive redirection hijack capabilities.

title: Exploitation of network services
hypothesis: An attacker exploited a network service (SMB/RDP/WinRM) vulnerability for movement.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4625 | where LogonType == 3 | where IpAddress !endswith '.0' | summarize count() by IpAddress | where count_ > 50
rationale: Failure bursts against services = exploit attempt trail.

title: WinRM/PSRemoting execution
hypothesis: An attacker used WinRM to run commands remotely.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessParentName == 'WmiPrvSE.exe' | where FileName == 'powershell.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'Remoting' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'WinRM'
rationale: WinRM-sourced PowerShell = remote exec.

title: Proxy/port-forward setup
hypothesis: An attacker forwarded internal ports through a compromised host.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('netsh.exe','ssh.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'portproxy' or ProcessCommandLine contains '-L '
rationale: portproxy/SSH tunneling = movement infrastructure.

title: Internal phishing
hypothesis: An attacker sent phishing from inside the network to another user.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4688 | where ProcessName == 'outlook.exe' | where CommandLine contains '/c'
rationale: Outlook launching shell = internal phishing/vba abuse.

title: Compressed payload over share
hypothesis: An attacker compressed tools and moved them over SMB.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 5145 | where RelativeTargetName endswith '.zip' or RelativeTargetName endswith '.7z'
rationale: Archives in shares = tool staging.

title: COM inter-process movement
hypothesis: An attacker used COM objects across processes to execute.
queries: DeviceEvents | where ActionType == 'ComObject' | where ObjectName contains 'InternetExplorer' or ObjectName contains 'ShellWindows'
rationale: Unusual COM activation from scripts = lateral capability.

title: SSH from admin workstation
hypothesis: An attacker pivoted Linux-to-Linux via SSH from a jump host.
queries: SecurityEvent | where Channel == 'auth' | where CommandLine contains 'ssh ' | where User != 'root'
rationale: SSH logons from non-admin user to many hosts = pivot.

title: Sensitive file collection
hypothesis: An attacker collected documents/credentials from user profiles.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FolderPath contains '\\Desktop' or FolderPath contains '\\Documents' | where FileName endswith ('.pst','.ost','.xlsx','.docx','.zip') | where ActionType == 'FileCopied' | where InitiatingProcessFileName in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe')
rationale: Copy-doc actions from shells = collection.

title: Mailbox search
hypothesis: An attacker searched mailboxes for sensitive keywords.
queries: AuditLogs | where Operation == 'Search-Mailbox' or Operation == 'MailItemsAccessed' | where ResultType == 'success'
rationale: Unusual mailbox search ops = email theft.

title: Archive collection
hypothesis: An attacker archived data dirs for exfil (zip creation).
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('7z.exe','rar.exe','winrar.exe','tar.exe') | where LocalAppDataFolder has 'Temp' or ProcessCommandLine contains '\\Users\\'
rationale: Archive tools on endpoints = collection stage.

title: Screen capture
hypothesis: An attacker captured screenshots of the desktop.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName endswith ('.png','.jpg','.bmp') | where FolderPath contains 'Temp' or FolderPath contains 'AppData' | where ActionType == 'FileCreated'
rationale: Fresh images in temp from unknown process = screenshots.

title: Clipboard capture
hypothesis: An attacker read the clipboard for secrets.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'Get-Clipboard' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'GetText'
rationale: Clipboard read commands from odd processes.

title: Remote email API use for bulk access
hypothesis: An attacker used Graph/EWS APIs to pull mail at volume.
queries: SigninLogs | where AppDisplayName has_any ('Microsoft Graph','Office 365 Exchange Online') | where UserAgent contains 'python' or UserAgent contains 'curl'
rationale: Scripted API mailbox access = bulk email theft.

title: HTTP/S beacon
hypothesis: A host communicates with C2 over HTTP/S on a fixed cadence.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteUrl startswith 'http' | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'chrome.exe' | summarize count() by InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m) | where count_ >= 10
rationale: Regular intervals to same URL from odd process.

title: Encrypted custom protocol on odd port
hypothesis: An attacker established a custom encrypted channel on a non-standard port.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemotePort !in (80, 443, 53) | where RemotePort < 1024 | where InitiatingProcessFileName in (sysProcesses) and InitiatingProcessFileName not in (svchost)
rationale: System processes on unusual ports = covert channel.

title: DGA domain resolution
hypothesis: Malware resolved algorithmically generated domains.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where ActionType == 'DnsQuery' | where RemoteUrl matches regex @'^[a-z0-9]{15,}\.' | where RemoteUrl endswith ('.top','.xyz','.ru','.icu')
rationale: High-entropy long subdomains on cheap TLDs = DGA.

title: File download via C2 channel
hypothesis: A C2 channel was used to pull additional tools.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName endswith ('.exe','.dll','.ps1') | where ActionType == 'FileCreated' | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'browser' | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'svchost.exe'
rationale: Non-browser binary fetches = tool delivery.

title: DNS tunneling
hypothesis: Malware exfiltrated/beaconed via DNS queries to a controlled domain.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where ActionType == 'DnsQuery' | where RemoteUrl endswith '.example.net' | where strlen(RemoteUrl) > 40
rationale: Long subdomain queries to one domain = DNS tunnel.

title: Remote access tool install
hypothesis: An attacker installed RAT/remote-control software for persistent access.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('teamviewer.exe','anydesk.exe','remoteutilities.exe','mremoteng.exe') | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'explorer.exe'
rationale: RAT install from non-user context.

title: Encoded command exfil over HTTP
hypothesis: C2 used base64-encoded parameters in HTTP requests.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteUrl contains 'http' | where RemoteUrl contains '=' | where UrlExtension contains 'php' or UrlExtension contains 'asp'
rationale: Query-string payloads to script endpoints = C2 encoding.

title: Mail protocols as C2
hypothesis: An attacker used SMTP/IMAP (mail) as a covert C2 channel.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemotePort in (25, 587, 993, 143) | where InitiatingProcessFileName not in ('outlook.exe','mapisvc')
rationale: Non-client processes talking mail ports = mail C2.

title: Web service C2 (pastebin/GitHub)
hypothesis: C2 used public web services to host content (pastebin, gist, raw URLs).
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteUrl has_any ('pastebin.com','gist.github.com','raw.githubusercontent.com') | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'browser'
rationale: Public-service fetches from odd processes = stager.

title: Raw TCP/UDP non-HTTP
hypothesis: A beacon uses raw sockets (non-HTTP) for C2.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where ActionType == 'OutboundConnection' | where RemotePort not in (80,443,53,3389,445,22) | summarize count() by RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName | where count_ >= 20
rationale: Persistent odd-port connections = raw C2.

title: External proxy use
hypothesis: Malware routes traffic via an open proxy it controls.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemotePort in (3128, 8080, 1080) | where RemoteIP !in (corporateProxies)
rationale: Non-corporate proxy ports = C2 redirector.

title: FTP-based exfil/beacon
hypothesis: An attacker used FTP for payload movement.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemotePort == 21 | where RemoteIP !in (ftpAllowlist)
rationale: FTP from non-admin hosts = traffic channel.

title: Data exfiltration over HTTP POST
hypothesis: Large volumes of internal data leaving over HTTP/S.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where Direction == 'Outbound' | where RemoteUrl startswith 'http' | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'browser' | where ActionType == 'ConnectionSuccess' | summarize bytes=count() by RemoteUrl | where bytes > 1000
rationale: Bulk POST volume signal (needs byte counts from proxy).

title: Exfil to cloud storage
hypothesis: Data was uploaded to personal cloud storage (Dropbox, Google Drive, MEGA).
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteUrl has_any ('dropbox.com','drive.google.com','mega.nz','wetransfer.com') | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'browser'
rationale: Non-browser upload to personal cloud = exfil.

title: Exfil to paste service
hypothesis: An attacker pasted sensitive data to pastebin-like services.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteUrl has_any ('pastebin.com','bit.ly','tinyurl.com')
rationale: Paste/URL-shortener use by unknown processes.

title: Exfil via DNS TXT
hypothesis: Data was exfiltrated in DNS TXT records to attacker domain.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where ActionType == 'DnsQuery' | where QueryType == 'TXT' | where RemoteUrl !endswith '.example.com' and strlen(RemoteUrl) > 60
rationale: Long TXT queries = DNS-based exfil.

title: Automated exfil (scheduled)
hypothesis: A scheduled task uploads data on a regular cadence.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'schtasks.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains '/create' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'powershell' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'curl'
rationale: Scheduled task wrapping network tools = automated exfil.

title: Data transfer size anomaly
hypothesis: A host suddenly transferred unusually large volumes.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where Direction == 'Outbound' | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'browser' | summarize bytes=count() by InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) | where bytes > 500000
rationale: Volume anomalies from single process = exfil burst.

title: Ransomware file extension surge
hypothesis: Many files were renamed/changed to ransomware extensions in a short window.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName endswith ('.lockbit','.enc','.crypt','.hive','.8lock8') | summarize count() by Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m) | where count_ > 50
rationale: Mass extension change = encryption in progress.

title: Backup/VSS destruction
hypothesis: An attacker disabled backups and deleted shadow copies.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ('vssadmin delete shadows','wmic shadowcopy delete','bcdedit /set recoveryenabled')
rationale: Backup destruction = ransomware precursor.

title: Mass file deletion
hypothesis: An attacker deleted large volumes of user data.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where ActionType == 'FileDeleted' | summarize count() by InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(TimeGenerated, 15m) | where count_ > 500
rationale: Mass deletion bursts = destructive impact.

title: Resource exhaustion DoS
hypothesis: A host was used to flood internal/external targets.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where ActionType == 'OutboundConnection' | where RemotePort not in (80,443,53) | where InitiatingProcessFileName in (sysProcesses) and InitiatingProcessFileName != 'svchost.exe' | summarize count() by RemoteIP | where count_ > 1000
rationale: Volumetric odd-port traffic = DoS participation.

title: Data manipulation (defacement)
hypothesis: An attacker modified web content or databases.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FolderPath contains 'inetpub' or FolderPath contains 'wwwroot' | where ActionType in ('FileModified','FileCreated') | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'w3wp.exe'
rationale: Non-server writes to web root = defacement.

title: ShadowPage/sysvol tampering
hypothesis: An attacker corrupted core system state (sysvol, GPOs).
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 5136 | where ObjectName contains 'Sysvol' | where OperationType contains 'Modify'
rationale: Sysvol changes outside GPO change windows = state tampering.

title: Domain admin session enumeration
hypothesis: An attacker enumerated active admin sessions to plan token theft.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'net session' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'qwinsta' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'query session'
rationale: Session enumeration = token/credential targeting.

title: Window/desktop enumeration
hypothesis: An attacker enumerated open windows/screens for interception or screenshots.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'powershell.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'Get-Process' and ProcessCommandLine contains 'MainWindowTitle'
rationale: Window-title enumeration = screen/UI interception prep.

title: Printer/Share discovery (spooler abuse prep)
hypothesis: An attacker queried the print spooler for later exploitation.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'spooler' and (ProcessCommandLine contains 'query' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'enum')
rationale: Spooler enumeration precedes PrintNightmare-class abuse.

title: Accessibility feature binary replacement
hypothesis: An attacker replaced sethc/Utilman with cmd for login-prompt persistence.
queries: DeviceFileEvents | where FileName in ('sethc.exe','utilman.exe','magnify.exe') | where ActionType in ('FileModified','FileCreated') | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'dism.exe'
rationale: Replacing accessibility binaries = classic elevator persistence.

title: Password filter DLL installation
hypothesis: An attacker installed a password filter to harvest password changes.
queries: DeviceRegistryEvents | where RegistryKey contains 'LSA\\Notification Packages' | where RegistryValueData contains '.dll' | where RegistryValueData !contains 'scecli'
rationale: LSA notification packages = password-change harvesting.

title: Port Monitor persistence
hypothesis: An attacker registered a port monitor DLL for print-spooler persistence.
queries: DeviceRegistryEvents | where RegistryKey contains '\\Print\\Monitors' | where RegistryValueData contains '.dll'
rationale: Print monitors autoload DLLs as SYSTEM.

title: XDG autostart (Linux desktop)
hypothesis: An attacker added a .desktop autostart entry on Linux.
queries: AuditdLogs | where type == 'PATH' | where name contains 'autostart' and name endswith '.desktop'
rationale: Desktop autostart entries = user-persistence on Linux.

title: Exploitation for client execution (browser/app)
hypothesis: A client-side exploit (browser, PDF, office) executed on a workstation.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName in ('acrord32.exe','chrome.exe','msedge.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'rundll32' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'powershell'
rationale: Client apps spawning shells = exploit chain.

title: Signed script execution (Msiexec/others)
hypothesis: An attacker ran signed utilities (msiexec, regsvr32) with payloads.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'msiexec.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'http' or ProcessCommandLine contains '\\\\'
rationale: msiexec remote/UNC install = signed-script abuse.

title: Regsvr32 scriptlet execution
hypothesis: regsvr32 ran a remote scriptlet (web delivery).
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'regsvr32.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'scrobj.dll'
rationale: regsvr32 scrobj.dll = scriptlet execution.

title: Shared module execution
hypothesis: An attacker executed code via exported functions of shared modules.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName == 'rundll32.exe' | where ProcessCommandLine contains ',Export' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'Control_RunDLL'
rationale: rundll32 export invocation = module-based execution.

title: Credentials in memory of RDP clients
hypothesis: An attacker dumped credentials from Password Manager / RDP clients memory.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName in ('mstsc.exe','creddump','ProcDump') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'mstsc' and ProcessCommandLine contains 'saved'
rationale: RDP client memory dumps = saved-credential extraction.

title: Bash history credential search
hypothesis: An attacker mined bash history files for passwords/keys.
queries: AuditdLogs | where type == 'SYSCALL' | where exe == '/usr/bin/tail' and cwd contains '/root' or exe == '/bin/cat' and name endswith '.bash_history'
rationale: History reads during lateral movement = credential harvest.

title: Cached credentials dump
hypothesis: An attacker attempted to extract cached domain credentials (MSCash).
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'cachedump' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'lsadump'
rationale: Cache-dump tool names in process tree.

title: Password manager vault access
hypothesis: An attacker accessed password manager vaults (LastPass, KeePass, 1Password).
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName in ('KeePass.exe','1Password.exe','LastPass.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'dump' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'export'
rationale: Vault tools with export/dump args = vault theft.

title: GUI input capture (RDP inject)
hypothesis: An attacker hooked desktop GUI input (keyboard) on a server.
queries: DeviceImageLoadEvents | where FileName contains 'hook' | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'explorer.exe' and FolderPath contains 'Users\\'
rationale: User-dir hook DLLs into sessions = GUI capture.

title: Pass-the-cache (Kerberos cache use)
hypothesis: An attacker used cached Kerberos tickets from memory.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4769 | where IpAddress != '::1' | where AccountName == 'SYSTEM'
rationale: SYSTEM-account service requests from workstations = ticket reuse.

title: Config management tool abuse (Ansible/Chef)
hypothesis: An attacker abused configuration-management push for code exec.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('ansible-playbook','chef-client','puppet') | where ProcessCommandLine contains 'sudo' or ProcessCommandLine contains 'run'
rationale: Config-push utilities as exec channel = expected only by ops teams.

title: Exploit attempts against SMB (EternalBlue family)
hypothesis: SMB exploit attempts (MS17-010) were made against internal hosts.
queries: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 5145 or EventID == 5140 | where RelativeTargetName contains 'IPC$' | where IpAddress !in (knownPatchMgmt)
rationale: IPC$ access + fail patterns = SMB exploit probing.

title: Remote copy via xcopy/robocopy
hypothesis: An attacker used xcopy/robocopy to push files laterally.
queries: DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has_any ('xcopy.exe','robocopy.exe') | where ProcessCommandLine contains '\\\\'
rationale: UNC-target copies = lateral file staging.

title: Internal proxy rotation
hypothesis: An attacker used internal hosts as C2 relay hops.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteIP in (internalRanges) | where RemotePort in (8080, 3128, 1080) | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'browser'
rationale: Internal proxy ports from odd processes = internal relay.

title: One-way C2 via web storage (Google Docs/Forms)
hypothesis: Malware uses Google Docs/Forms or similar as dead-drop resolvers.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteUrl has_any ('docs.google.com','forms.gle','api.telegram.org') | where InitiatingProcessFileName not in ('chrome.exe','msedge.exe','outlook.exe')
rationale: Dead-drop resolver endpoints from odd processes.

title: Domain fronting
hypothesis: An attacker used domain fronting (HTTPS host header mismatch) for C2.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteUrl startswith 'https://' | where InitiatingProcessFileName != 'browser' | where ActionType == 'DnsQuery' and RemoteUrl !endswith proxyAllowedDomains
rationale: HTTPS resolvers that aren't allowed destinations = fronting.

title: Multi-stage beacon check-in pattern
hypothesis: Malware performs staged check-ins (short-then-long) to evade blocking.
queries: DeviceNetworkEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName in (suspectedBeacons) | summarize min(TimeGenerated), max(TimeGenerated), count() by RemoteIP | extend delta = max - min | where delta > 1d and count() < 50
rationale: Sparse-but-persistent connections = staged beacon.
